# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: training after the first risk treatment, before the statement of
  applicability gets written
- Audience: `practitioners`
- Length: 45 minutes, with a shared mapping exercise on a real row from your own
  risk register
- What the audience already knows: a finished treatment, and the terms control,
  residual risk and statement of applicability

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. There is a second deck for this topic, for
engineering. It is not the shorter version of this one: it starts at a single
number, this one at the order of the procedure.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27002 says what stands behind the numbers of the annex, and this
standard is used from the treatment and not from the list.

## Why it concerns the practitioners

- The statement of applicability is written by the practitioners, and it stands
  in the audit later
- What is required is the comparison against the annex, ISO/IEC 27001:2022,
  6.1.3, and not the application of every number
- Anyone starting with the list makes an inventory that looks like an ISMS

# The direction

## From the treatment to the number

- After the treatment it stands for every risk what is to be done
- For every intention the number it stands under in the annex is looked for
- Usually one, sometimes two, occasionally none

## When no number fits

- That is not a mistake but a control of your own
- It stands in the risk register and not in the statement of applicability
- That statement is built against the annex and not against the organisation

# The comparison

## What the comparison really is

- Going through the annex once over its whole length
- Asking for every number: does this concern a risk we have missed
- It is a check against what was forgotten and not a promise of completeness

## Two outcomes and no third

- Application with a reason that points back to a risk row
- Non-application with a reason that is a finding about the risk situation
- An empty row is neither, and that is exactly what an audit looks for

# Where it tips

## Three mistakes that look like proper work

- The comparison before the treatment: the reasons then come from the standard
  instead of from your own situation
- Non-application reasoned by the effort: effort is a reason to treat
  differently and not a statement about the risk
- The old mapping carried on: the 2022 edition is rebuilt, and a number from the
  2013 edition points somewhere else

## What stands in the statement at the end

- For every number of the annex a decision with a reason
- Date and person responsible
- Beside it your own controls that do not occur in the annex

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The next steps

- Carry one treated row through in full, until two reasoned numbers stand there
- Take the template in `templates/soa` and put no fields of your own beside it
- Collect the non-applications whose reason sounds like effort and hold them
  against the risk situation
- Who, by when: belongs in the discussion and not on this slide

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27002:2022, as a whole standard
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 8.1, 8.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1
- ISO/IEC 27005:2022, as a whole standard

No standard wording, no control title and no enumeration of the annex numbers
stands on these slides. No clause number of ISO/IEC 27002 is named, and the
reason stands in the chapter on that standard.
